unmapped_findings: For the 1050→950 °C, 0.01 s^-1 (0.4 strain) condition, the temperature decrease occurs over a 0.1 strain interval; the strengthening work hardening raises the experimental stress and, at the end of the temperature decrease, a new second-stage peak appears that is lower than the constant-condition value, with a greater ε_I (0.4 vs 0.2) giving a lower second-stage peak stress.
After the second-stage peak in the 1050→950 °C (0.4 strain) condition, the flow stress decreases briefly and then rises significantly because of interfacial friction (Fig. 9).

The decreasing-temperature condition leaves first-stage DRX grains (DRXGs_I) that are not fully refined because second-stage DRX grain nucleation is delayed; at 0.9 strain the residual DRXGs_I are larger (63.29 µm, VF 0.37) than the constant-condition AGS (52.52 µm), enlarging the final AGS to 58.30 µm (Table 6).

Fig. 22b/22d compare DRX fraction and average dislocation density evolution for decreasing temperature 1050→950 °C in the 0.4–0.5 strain range at 0.01 s^-1, but no numeric curve values are printed in the available image description.
